We endeavour to be a ‘Reading School’
At Hunton CE Primary School, we believe reading is the foundation of learning and consequently at the heart of the curriculum.
To engage pupils into reading, each class, every term has a class novel from which to teach reading skills from. Class teachers select engaging and rich texts to immerse pupils into new worlds, as well as using texts to support wider curriculum learning. The school has two libraries to further foster a love for reading.
Pupils learn reading progressively, using our Reading Skills Progression Booklet available.

What are Modern Foreign Languages?
Modern Foreign Languages encompass all languages, aside from English, which are spoken and used in different countries around the world. The term ‘Modern Languages’ is used to distinguish between the languages spoken today and ‘Classical languages’. Therefore, ‘Modern languages’ do not include languages such as Latin or Ancient Greek because they are no longer commonly practised.
Modern Foreign Languages are a mandatory component of the British state education system up until KS3, or S3 in Scotland. Schools can choose what languages they teach, though most choose European languages like French, German and Spanish.

SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disability) Information
At Hunton CE Primary School, we pride ourselves on providing an inclusive, nurturing environment, where all children are valued, respected and welcomed to the school, whatever their additional educational need. We will support their learning and wellbeing, enable them to take a full and active part in all school activities and support them to thrive and achieve their full potential.
The staff at Hunton recognise that all children in their care are unique. We take time to make sure we know all our children well and strive to ensure that the needs of each individual child are met. Every child has access to a broad and balanced curriculum, enriched with a variety of hands on learning activities in our beautiful school grounds and surrounding area.
We use a graduated response to meet the needs of our pupils, founded on the principle of high quality, inclusive classroom teaching as the foundation of our support for every child. To achieve this, we use the mainstream core standards to guide the planning of our provision in each class.
More information about the support that we offer for pupils with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) can be found in our SEND policy. This document is regularly updated and sets out the school’s systems for identification, assessment, supporting, monitoring, reviewing and evaluating provision for pupils with SEND.
Our policy fully supports the 2014 SEND Code of Practice; Inclusive Schooling of Children with Special Education Needs and the Disability Rights Code of Practice for Schools.
Any concerns you may have about your child should be shared with your child’s class teacher, as they will usually know your child best. The class teacher may then seek advice and support from the school’s Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Co-ordinator (SENDCo).
The SENDCo at Hunton CE Primary School is Mrs Wichall. She is usually in school on Tuesdays. You can contact Mrs Wichall via the school office or on the contact us page of the website.
For further information about the SEND support and services available in Kent,

Clubs
The after-school clubs at Hunton C of E Primary School
Our school’s after-school clubs try to offer something for everyone, creating a space where students can explore their passions, build new skills, and connect with friends outside the classroom. From sports teams that encourage teamwork and fitness, to creative outlets like craft clubs and music, there is a wide variety of opportunities to get involved. These clubs not only provide fun and relaxation after a busy school day, but they also help students discover new interests and strengthen our sense of community. Whether you’re looking to compete, create, or simply try something new, the after-school program is a chance to grow while having a great time.
Previous sports clubs have included football, netball, acro, tennis and dance. Arts and crafts clubs are for everyone to enjoy but some clubs, such as Creepy Claws are not for the faint hearted!
The Family Trust run a free Christian based after school club teaching children bible stories and the message of Christ in a fun and interactive environment.

Governors’ Information and Duties
What the Governors do
The board of governors work hard to ensure the aims of Hunton CEP School are met. The principle duty of a governor is to contribute to the continuing improvement of the school through a wide variety of activities.
As a body they are responsible for setting the direction for the school. Our governors work tirelessly to review and monitor the work of the school in line with strategic direction as well as ensuring that we meet all statutory responsibilities.
Our governors are ‘critical friends’ to our school which facilitates the raising of standards and supports areas for development. The governing body develops policies and plans which reflect the aims and strategic goals of the school.
Hunton CEP School has main board meetings and committees which have responsibility for maintenance and improvement of the school building, deciding how the budget is spent and by encouraging good home school and community partnerships. Should you wish to view governor minutes, please request the clerk of governors via the school office.
The Headteacher is responsible for the day to day running of the school, including staff management, implementing policies and monitoring the learning and teaching.
If you would be interested in becoming a governor of our school please contact our Chair of Governors through the school office.
